findings.title: Google Calendar refresh persists the safeParse wrapper object instead of the parsed data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns a Zod safeParse-style object `{ success, data }`. Here the whole return value is assigned to `key` and stored directly as `data: { key }` in `prisma.credential.update`. Every other integration in this PR (Office365, Zoom, Webex, Salesforce) correctly destructures `.data` before persisting, but Google does not. As a result, every time a Google Calendar access token is refreshed (which happens routinely as tokens expire), `credential.key` in the DB becomes `{ success: true, data: { access_token, refresh_token, ... } }` instead of the flat object expected by `googleCredentialSchema`. The next call to `googleAuth()` does `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`, which will throw because the stored object no longer has the required top-level fields. This permanently breaks the Google Calendar integration for the account after the first refresh, for all users (not just self-hosters using the new sync feature).

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" instead of a real value
findings.body: When the parsed token response lacks a `refresh_token` field, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` — a hardcoded placeholder string, not a variable. This path runs unconditionally (both in the sync and non-sync branches). For integrations whose schema marks `refresh_token` optional (e.g. Office365's `refreshTokenResponseSchema`), if the provider's refresh response omits a new refresh_token, this garbage string gets merged into the credential object and persisted to the DB (e.g. `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), silently destroying the previously valid refresh_token. Subsequent refresh attempts will send the literal string "refresh_token" to the OAuth provider and fail, permanently breaking the calendar connection until the user reconnects.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed property keys collapse to the same literal key, defeating the intended schema
findings.body: The schema uses computed property names `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Calling `.toString()` on a Zod type instance does not return the string "any string"; it returns the default `Object.prototype.toString()` result, i.e. the literal string `"[object Object]"`, for both expressions. The two computed keys collide into one key named `"[object Object]"`, which never matches any real response property. The comments ("Assume that any property with a number is the expiry", "Allow other properties") indicate the intent was to keep arbitrary/expiry fields, but because `z.object()` strips unrecognized keys by default, the parsed result of `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse()` only ever retains `access_token` (plus the refresh_token fallback). This means when credential syncing is enabled, fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` are silently stripped from the refreshed credential before being persisted, breaking expiry tracking for every app that relies on this schema (Google Calendar in particular).

findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a different response shape depending on branch, breaking several consumers when credential sync is enabled
findings.body: When the sync feature is active, this function returns the raw Fetch API `Response` object from `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`. When it is not active, it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` resolves to. For Google Calendar, `refreshFunction` resolves to a gaxios-style object exposing `.data` (via `fetchTokens.res`), and the caller does `const token = res?.data; token.access_token`. A raw Fetch `Response` has no `.data` property, so when the sync endpoint is configured this throws/returns `undefined.access_token`. The same mismatch exists for Hubspot (caller expects `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` from the Hubspot SDK's token object, not a Fetch Response), and for Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM (caller expects `tokenInfo.data` as returned by axios, not a Fetch Response). This means the exact feature this PR introduces (syncing credentials via `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) will throw or silently break for Google Calendar, Hubspot, Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM as soon as it is enabled.

findings.title: Outbound credential-sync request carries no authentication/secret header
findings.body: When calling out to the self-hoster's `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, the request is a plain POST with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body — no signature, bearer token, or shared secret (e.g. `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) is sent. The self-hosted endpoint therefore has no built-in way to verify that the request genuinely originated from this Cal.com instance, unlike the inbound `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint, which does require a shared secret. This is a one-sided trust model: any party that can reach the configured endpoint URL can impersonate Cal.com's refresh requests unless the self-hoster independently reinvents authentication, which is not documented anywhere in `.env.example`.

findings.title: credential.id is passed to refreshOAuthTokens where credential.userId is expected
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken(credentialId: number, credentialKey: BiginToken)` only has access to `credentialId` (`credential.id`), not `credential.userId`; there is no `userId` variable in scope. The call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` therefore passes the credential's primary key as the third argument, which `refreshOAuthTokens` treats as `userId` and sends to the self-hosted sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. When credential syncing is enabled for Zoho Bigin, the self-hoster's endpoint will receive the wrong identifier and will be unable to correctly map the request to the Cal.com user, breaking token refresh for this app specifically.

findings.title: Salesforce access token is unconditionally refreshed on every service instantiation, without an expiry check or the new sync mechanism
findings.body: `getClient()` is invoked from the constructor on every `SalesforceCalendarService` instantiation (i.e. on essentially every booking/calendar operation for a Salesforce credential), and it unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` to refresh the access token — there is no check of token expiry before doing so, unlike every other integration in this codebase (which gate refreshing behind an `isExpired`/`isTokenValid` check). This wastes Salesforce API quota on every call and, since Salesforce issues/may rotate refresh tokens, repeated unnecessary refreshes under concurrent requests can race and invalidate tokens still in use elsewhere. Additionally, unlike all the other apps touched in this PR, this refresh call is not routed through the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, so the self-hosted credential-sync feature this PR introduces does not work for Salesforce at all, despite the PR's stated goal of broad app support.

findings.title: Webhook secret verified with non-constant-time string comparison and no HTTP method restriction
findings.body: The webhook secret check uses plain `!==` comparison between the incoming header value and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is vulnerable to timing side-channel attacks that can be used to guess the secret byte-by-byte, especially since the endpoint has no rate limiting. A constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) should be used instead. Additionally, the handler does not check `req.method`, so non-POST requests are processed the same way; a GET/other request without a JSON body will fail the zod `.parse()` with an unhandled exception rather than a clean 405, leaking a generic error instead of a well-defined API contract.

findings.title: Decrypted credential payload is persisted without any schema validation
findings.body: After `symmetricDecrypt` + `JSON.parse`, the resulting `keys` object is written straight into `prisma.credential.create/update` as the `key` field, with no validation that it matches the shape expected by the corresponding app's CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter (e.g. `googleCredentialSchema`, `zoomTokenSchema`, etc.). A malformed or incomplete payload from the self-hosted sync source (missing `refresh_token`, wrong types, etc.) will be accepted and stored, and will only fail later — at booking/availability time — when the relevant integration tries to `schema.parse(credential.key)`, causing a runtime exception far removed from the original cause. There is also no try/catch around the decrypt/JSON.parse calls, so a bad payload or wrong encryption key results in an unhandled exception rather than a clear 4xx response.

findings.title: Redirect URI hardcoded, diverging from appConfig.slug used in callback.ts
findings.body: This change replaces `WEBAPP_URL + \`/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback\`` with a hardcoded `WEBAPP_URL + "/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback"`. `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/callback.ts` still builds its redirect URI from `appConfig.slug`. The two files are now inconsistent: if `appConfig.slug` in `config.json` ever changes, the authorize URL and the token-exchange redirect URI would silently diverge, breaking the OAuth flow for this app. This change appears unrelated to the credential-sync feature and looks like an unintended regression introduced by the refactor.

findings.title: No automated tests for the new credential-sync webhook or OAuth refresh-sync code paths
findings.body: This PR adds a new unauthenticated-by-default webhook endpoint that decrypts and writes arbitrary third-party OAuth credentials into the database, plus new shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that are wired into nearly a dozen app integrations' token-refresh logic. None of this is covered by unit or integration tests (the PR description explicitly states no tests were added). Given the security sensitivity (webhook secret, symmetric encryption/decryption) and the data-integrity risk (credential corruption as seen in the bugs above), this is a significant gap that would have caught the shape-mismatch and placeholder-value bugs before merge.
